task.description:

This is a docs/protocol design (no @spec/module interface) -- your bar is: every ISS-0467.yaml acceptance criterion is covered by a concrete design element, the option choice (Option 2, prohibition) is honestly justified against ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis rather than asserted, the exact verbatim text for both GIT_MERGE.md and ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 is unambiguous enough to apply without further judgement calls, no implementation code is present, and the reasoning about ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 (whether the sizing rule as currently written already prohibits a bare push, and whether a correction is still needed) is independently checked against the actual text of sec.10 and AGENT_SYSTEM.md sec.4 -- re-derive this yourself by reading those two sections directly, do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's characterization of them on trust. Check placement instructions are unambiguous (exact insertion points named). Check AC3's claim that nothing regresses the gh pr merge/--admin path -- verify by reading GIT_MERGE.md's actual Step 8 and confirming the design proposes no edit to it.

REGATE (iteration 1): your prior FAIL (gate_history[0]) found exactly 1 BLOCKER -- design section 7 mislabeled its 3 acceptance criteria as verbatim from docs/issues/ISS-0467.yaml, which has no such field. ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 and AGENT_SYSTEM.md sec.4 read directly by you; confirm or refute the design's claim that neither currently licenses a bare push to main
GIT_MERGE.md verbatim insertion text and location instructions are unambiguous -- confirm the named insertion point actually exists at the stated location in the current file
ORCHESTRATOR.md sec.10 verbatim insertion text and location instructions are unambiguous -- confirm the named insertion point actually exists at the stated location in the current file
No implementation code (.ex/.exs bodies) present anywhere in the design artefact
AC3 regression claim verified by reading GIT_MERGE.md Step 8 directly and confirming no edit to it is proposed
Decision-record placement (amend 0018 in place vs new record) reasoning checked against 0018's own 'What this record does not decide' and 'Follow-up' sections
